name: Hegra Archaeological Site (al-Hijr / Madā ͐ in Ṣāliḥ)
description: Hegra, also called Mada'in Salih, sits in the desert near Al-'Ula in northwestern Saudi Arabia. It was the Nabataeans' second city after Petra, and 111 tombs were carved into its sandstone outcrops about 2,000 years ago, most with ornate decorated facades. Dry air and centuries of abandonment kept them remarkably intact, along with the ancient wells that sustained this desert trading outpost.
